note: DRAFT v1 module checks and final designation exam for the CARSI Contaminated-Water Practitioner course. Original CARSI questions written for Australian and New Zealand conditions; no IICRC standard text reproduced. SME review and sign-off required before seeding.

questions.questionText: A blocked sewer main surcharges through a floor waste. Which category is the water?
options: Category 1, clean supply
Category 2, slightly used
Category 3, grossly contaminated
Uncategorised until lab tested
questions.explanation: Sewage from a surcharging sewer is a Category 3 source. You call it from the source and its history; you do not wait for a lab result to protect people.

questions.questionText: The evidence on site is mixed between Category 2 and Category 3. What do you do?
options: Call Category 3 and record why
Call Category 2 to save time
Average them and call it 2.5
Wait a week and look again
questions.explanation: When unsure, call the worse category and write down your reasons. Under-calling black water as grey can make people sick; over-calling mainly costs some efficiency.

questions.questionText: Why does the category matter more than the volume of water?
options: It sets the price per litre
It decides only the drying time
It names the insurer to call
It decides the method and PPE
questions.explanation: Contamination, not the amount of water, decides the method: risk assessment, PPE, removal, cleaning, disposal and then drying.

questions.questionText: How do leptospirosis bacteria get into the body?
options: Only by drinking treated town tap water
Through cuts, open wounds, eyes, nose, mouth
Only through intact and completely dry skin
Only by touching clean and dry timber
questions.explanation: Queensland Government advice: leptospirosis bacteria get in through cuts, open wounds, or the eyes, nose or mouth. Cover cuts with waterproof dressings and wear eye protection.

questions.questionText: Which vaccines does the Australian Immunisation Handbook recommend for workers in regular contact with untreated sewage?
options: Hepatitis A and tetanus
Influenza and chickenpox only
Measles and rubella only
No vaccine is recommended
questions.explanation: The Handbook recommends hepatitis A and tetanus for plumbers and others in regular contact with untreated sewage. In New Zealand, hepatitis A is recommended (unfunded) for sewage workers. Your doctor or occupational health provider decides.

questions.questionText: A bathroom 2.4 m × 1.8 m and a hallway 6.0 m × 1.1 m are affected. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: 2.4 × 1.8 = 4.32 m² and 6.0 × 1.1 = 6.60 m²; 4.32 + 6.60 = 10.92 m². Area in m² feeds the extraction plan, PPE quantities and the job file.

questions.questionText: In New Zealand, who holds the primary duty of care for workers on a sewage job?
options: The homeowner
The PCBU
The insurer
The apprentice
questions.explanation: Under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, section 36, the PCBU must ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health and safety of its workers. Australia’s model WHS laws use the same idea.

questions.questionText: Under Australian model WHS laws, when is a SWMS required?
options: Only after an incident has happened
Only when an insurer requests it
Never, as it is optional paperwork
Before any high-risk construction work starts
questions.explanation: A SWMS must be prepared before high-risk construction work starts. Triggers on Category 3 jobs include disturbing asbestos, confined spaces, energised electrical work and contaminated atmospheres.

questions.questionText: A technician develops a serious infection after sewage work. In New Zealand, what must the PCBU do?
options: Notify WorkSafe as soon as possible
Wait for the worker to complain
Tell the insurer but not WorkSafe
Nothing, because infections are not notifiable
questions.explanation: HSWA section 23 includes a serious infection that work significantly contributed to, including contact with human bodily substances. The PCBU notifies WorkSafe as soon as possible and keeps a record for five years.

questions.questionText: A Christchurch house was built in 1994. What is the asbestos assumption before cutting linings?
options: No asbestos after 1990 in NZ
Asbestos only in the roof sheets
Assume asbestos until it is checked
Asbestos does not matter when wet
questions.explanation: WorkSafe New Zealand: any building built or renovated before 2000 could contain asbestos. In Australia, assume it in any building built or renovated before 31 December 2003, when the national ban took effect; those built or renovated before 1990 are the most likely to contain it. You cannot tell by looking.

questions.questionText: Why is a septic tank or sewer pit treated as a possible confined space?
options: It is too small to enter
It can hold hydrogen sulphide gas
It usually sits above the ground
It holds only clean rainwater now
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia’s confined-spaces code lists hydrogen sulphide build-up in sewers and pits, and methane displacing oxygen. Entry needs a trained crew, not a torch and good intentions.

questions.questionText: A wet ceiling stain is 3.0 m × 2.4 m holding 10 mm of water. About how much does that water weigh?
options: 72 kg
7.2 kg
720 kg
24 kg
questions.explanation: 3.0 × 2.4 = 7.2 m²; × 0.010 m = 0.072 m³ = 72 L. Water is about 1 kg per litre, so about 72 kg hangs over the room. Nobody works in the drop zone.

questions.questionText: A technician has a full beard. Which respirator choice is right?
options: A tight-fitting half-face respirator
A disposable dust mask
No respirator worn whatsoever
A hood-type powered respirator
questions.explanation: Facial hair stops a tight-fitting respirator from sealing. A respirator that does not rely on a face seal, such as a hood-type powered respirator, is used instead (SafeWork SA; WorkSafe New Zealand).

questions.questionText: How often does WorkSafe New Zealand recommend repeating a respirator fit test?
options: Only once, when the worker first starts
At least yearly, or after facial change
Every five years, done by the worker
Never, because a fit check covers it
questions.explanation: WorkSafe New Zealand recommends fit testing when the respirator is first provided and at least yearly, or after a significant facial change. In Australia, fit test before first use and after a facial change. Fit-check every time in both.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between a fit test and a fit check?
options: Test is formal; check is every wear
The two are exactly the same thing
Check is done once a year only
Test applies only to disposable dust masks
questions.explanation: A fit test is a formal test of seal on the wearer by a competent person. A fit check is the quick seal check the wearer does each time the respirator goes on.

questions.questionText: A technician has a cut on his knuckle. What happens before he starts?
options: Leave it open to air dry
Dab on sanitiser and then start
Cover it with a waterproof dressing
Work gloveless so he can watch
questions.explanation: Cuts are entry points for infection. Health authorities in both countries say to cover cuts with waterproof dressings before contact with floodwater, mud or sewage.

questions.questionText: In the transition zone, which item comes off last?
options: The outer gloves
The coverall suit
The work boots
The inner gloves
questions.explanation: Inner gloves come off last so your bare hands never touch the contaminated outside of the coverall, respirator or boots. Then wash hands and face.

questions.questionText: Where is strip-out waste bagged and sealed?
options: In the van, on the drive back home
In the transition zone, before the clean area
On the lounge carpet, to sort out later
At the tip, just before it is tipped
questions.explanation: Waste is bagged where it comes out and sealed in the transition zone, then taken out by the controlled route. Nothing contaminated crosses into the clean area unbagged.

questions.questionText: Why is containment set up before the carpet is pulled up?
options: Disturbance spreads it through the house
The carpet rolls up more easily
It stops the owner watching work
Containment is only for mould jobs
questions.explanation: Strip-out and extraction throw contamination into the air and onto surfaces. Containment first keeps it inside the work area.

questions.questionText: How can you see that negative pressure is working?
options: The AFD sounds louder than it did
The room smells more strongly than before
Doorway sheeting bows into the work area
The windows fog up on the outside
questions.explanation: When the AFD exhausts more air than leaks back in, the work area sits at lower pressure and the doorway sheeting bows inwards. Leaks then flow into the work area, not out.

questions.questionText: Why does Health New Zealand advise against water blasters on sewage-contaminated areas?
options: They use too much water overall
They damage the concrete surface badly
They work far too slowly overall
They spread contaminants into the air
questions.explanation: High-pressure water creates aerosols that carry contamination into the air you and others breathe. Low-aerosol methods are part of controlling the breathing route.

questions.questionText: Which material is usually removed and discarded after soaking in Category 3 water?
options: Carpet and underlay
Glazed ceramic tile
Stainless steel sink
Sealed concrete slab
questions.explanation: Porous materials such as carpet and underlay absorb contamination and cannot be verified clean, so they generally come out. Non-porous surfaces are usually cleaned and disinfected.

questions.questionText: Why is a surface cleaned before it is disinfected?
options: Cleaning makes disinfectant smell nicer
Disinfectant cannot work through dirt
Disinfecting first damages the floor
It only suits the photographs
questions.explanation: Cleaning removes soil, film and most organisms. Disinfectant cannot reach organisms protected under dirt. NSW Health and Health New Zealand both give the clean-then-disinfect order.

questions.questionText: In Australia, a hard-surface disinfectant claims to kill viruses. What does the TGA require?
options: Nothing, because any claim is allowed
Inclusion on the ARTG before supply
Only a registration number from overseas
Written approval from the local council
questions.explanation: A virucidal claim is a "specific claim". The TGA requires a disinfectant making a specific claim to be included in the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods before supply.

questions.questionText: A work area is 21.7 m² with a 2.4 m ceiling. What airflow gives 4 air changes per hour?
options: About 52 m³/h
About 87 m³/h
About 520 m³/h
About 208 m³/h
questions.explanation: 21.7 × 2.4 = 52.1 m³; × 4 = about 208 m³/h. The 4 air changes per hour target is an illustrative teaching figure; choose an AFD rated above it.

questions.questionText: A label says 1 part concentrate to 20 parts water. How much concentrate makes a 5 L batch?
options: About 25 mL
About 500 mL
About 240 mL
About 1 L
questions.explanation: A 1:20 dilution is 1 part in 21 parts total: 5 L ÷ 21 ≈ 0.24 L, about 240 mL, topped up with water to 5 L.

questions.questionText: What do you record for each disinfectant used?
options: Product, approval, dilution, contact time, area
Only the price and bottle colour
Only the product brand name shown
Nothing at all unless someone asks
questions.explanation: The product record is part of the defensible file: name, registration or approval, dilution, contact time and area treated, with the SDS held.

questions.questionText: Where does stormwater go in most Australian and New Zealand cities?
options: To a sewage treatment plant before release
Back into the town drinking water supply
Untreated to creeks, rivers and the sea
Into each building’s own private septic tank
questions.explanation: EPA Victoria and Watercare both say stormwater reaches waterways untreated. Category 3 water down a stormwater grate puts raw sewage into a waterway.

questions.questionText: A business wants to discharge extracted Category 3 water to the sewer in Victoria. What does it need?
options: A trade waste agreement with the authority
Nothing, because sewage may go to sewer
A signed note from the homeowner only
A written permit from the insurer only
questions.explanation: EPA Victoria: businesses need a trade waste agreement with the local water authority to discharge trade waste to a sewer. Other authorities have their own approvals; ask first.

questions.questionText: In Auckland, who controls trade waste discharges to the public wastewater system?
options: WorkSafe New Zealand inspectors
The Ministry of Health
The homeowner’s insurance company
Auckland Council, through Watercare
questions.explanation: Auckland’s Trade Waste Bylaw covers discharges to the public wastewater system and is managed by Watercare. Higher-risk trade waste needs a trade waste agreement.

questions.questionText: A broken drain under the slab caused the overflow. Who repairs it in New Zealand?
options: The restoration technician already on site
An authorised drainlayer or licensed plumber
The loss adjuster for the insurer
Any labourer with a good shovel
questions.explanation: Under the Plumbers, Gasfitters, and Drainlayers Act 2006, a person must not do sanitary plumbing or drainlaying unless authorised. In Australia it is licensed plumbing work.

questions.questionText: A grey fibrous backing is found under old vinyl in a 1960s house. What happens to it?
options: Stop work and call a licensed assessor
Put it in the general skip too
Snap it up and bag it quickly
Leave it there for the next owner
questions.explanation: Treat it as asbestos until checked. You cannot tell by looking, and in Australia a licence is needed to assess or remove asbestos. It never goes in the general skip.

questions.questionText: About 400 L of wastewater is extracted with a 45 L recovery tank. How many tank-loads is that?
options: 4 tank-loads
18 tank-loads
9 tank-loads
45 tank-loads
questions.explanation: 400 ÷ 45 = 8.9, so 9 tank-loads, each decanted into sealed drums for collection and logged on the wastewater record.

questions.questionText: On a Category 3 job, when do air movers go in?
options: Before anything is removed
As the crew arrives
Whenever the insurer asks
After cleaning is verified
questions.explanation: You dry a clean structure. Contain, remove, clean and disinfect, verify clean, then dry. Air movers across dirty material spread it.

questions.questionText: Mould is found behind a robe during drying. What changes?
options: More air movers aimed straight at it
AFDs and dehumidifiers only until the clearance
Nothing, so carry on as first planned
Bleach is sprayed on and left there
questions.explanation: The mould rule: no air movers across mouldy surfaces. Contain, run AFDs and dehumidifiers, remediate, and bring in air movers only after cleaning and clearance.

questions.questionText: Two dehumidifiers at 4.5 A and an AFD at 2.5 A run on 230 V. Can they share one 10 A circuit?
options: No, 11.5 A, so split them
Yes, 230 V allows any load
Yes, the RCD stops any overload
No, dehumidifiers each need 400 V
questions.explanation: 4.5 + 4.5 + 2.5 = 11.5 A, more than a 10 A circuit carries; the breaker would trip. Split the load across two circuits, each run through an RCD.

questions.questionText: Why does Queensland Health advise against dry brushing mould?
options: It is too slow for big jobs
It damages the paint finish on plasterboard
It can release spores into the air
It uses far too much detergent overall
questions.explanation: Dry brushing is abrasive and can release mould spores into the air. Use methods that do not spread spores, inside containment.

questions.questionText: What must a Category 3 clearance be based on?
options: How tidy the room looks to the owner
Recorded evidence that it is clean and dry
How the lead technician feels about the job
The finish date that the insurer has set
questions.explanation: Clearance is a decision made on evidence: porous material removed, surfaces visibly clean, cleaning recorded, readings at the dry standard, photographs, and a signed handover.

questions.questionText: Under New Zealand’s Consumer Guarantees Act, how must a service be carried out?
options: As cheaply as is possible
Exactly as the insurer says
Within one single working day
With reasonable care and skill
questions.explanation: The Consumer Guarantees Act requires services to be carried out with reasonable care and skill and to be fit for purpose. In Australia, the ACL requires due care and skill.

questions.questionText: Why are job records made at the time, not written up later?
options: They are more likely to be accepted
They take much less time to type
Insurers ban all notes made at home
They never need any photographs at all
questions.explanation: Records made as the work happens are the evidence a loss adjuster, regulator or court is most likely to accept. A file rebuilt from memory is weak evidence.

questions.questionText: An invoice is $4,800.00 ex GST in Australia. What is the total inc GST?
What is a common reason a practical submission is sent back?
options: Too many dated and captioned photos
No reason given for the category
Metric units are used throughout it
Every sum shows its working units
questions.explanation: The assessor needs your reasoning. A category with no reason, PPE without a fit test, or waste with no route or docket are common reasons for resubmission.

quizzes.title: CARSI Contaminated-Water Practitioner — Final designation exam

questions.questionText: Which of these is a Category 3 water source?
options: A burst cold-water pipe
A septic tank overflowing
A leaking rainwater tank
An overflowing clean bath
questions.explanation: A failed on-site wastewater system such as a septic tank is a Category 3 source. Clean supply water starts as Category 1, though it can worsen with time and contact.

questions.questionText: Floodwater from a river has entered a home in Hawke’s Bay. How should you treat it?
options: As clean because it came from rain
As grey water for the first week
As safe once the sun comes out
As contaminated with sewage and with chemicals
questions.explanation: Health New Zealand advises assuming floodwater is contaminated with farm run-off, animal and human sewage and chemicals. NSW Health gives the same warning in Australia.

questions.questionText: Which control mainly blocks the swallowing route?
options: Washing hands before eating or vaping
Wearing a fit-tested P2 respirator mask
Running an AFD with HEPA filters
Laying sheeting at the transition zone
questions.explanation: Hand-to-mouth contact is the swallowing route. Washing hands before eating, drinking, smoking or vaping blocks it; the respirator and AFD protect the breathing route.

questions.questionText: Which hepatitis A vaccine position is correct for New Zealand sewage workers?
options: Banned for all sewage workers
Funded for every adult worker
Recommended but unfunded, maybe employer-funded
Not mentioned in the Handbook
questions.explanation: The New Zealand Immunisation Handbook recommends hepatitis A, unfunded, for occupational groups exposed to faeces, including sewage workers, and notes it may be employer-funded.

questions.questionText: Under Australia’s model WHS Regulations, which infection can be a notifiable serious illness?
options: Any cold caught at home over winter
One from contact with human body substances
Only infections that a doctor diagnosed overseas
None, because only injuries are ever notifiable
questions.explanation: Regulation 699 lists infections significantly contributed to by work, including contact with human blood or body substances, and leptospirosis from animal waste.

questions.questionText: Which job feature is a high-risk construction work trigger for a SWMS in Australia?
options: Work done on a weekday
Work for a residential client
Work under a fixed quote
Work likely to disturb asbestos
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia lists work likely to disturb asbestos, in or near confined spaces, near energised electrical installations, or in a contaminated atmosphere among high-risk construction work.

questions.questionText: What is the New Zealand rule of thumb for asbestos in buildings?
options: Built or renovated before 2000
Built or renovated before 1950
Built or renovated before 1990
Built or renovated after 2010
questions.explanation: WorkSafe New Zealand: any building built or renovated before 2000 could contain asbestos. In Australia, assume it in any building built or renovated before 31 December 2003, when the national ban took effect; those built or renovated before 1990 are the most likely to contain it.

questions.questionText: Australian and New Zealand mains supply is nominally what?
options: 240 V at 60 Hz
400 V at 60 Hz
230 V at 50 Hz
24 V at 50 Hz
questions.explanation: Both countries supply a nominal 230 V at 50 Hz (NSW Government; NZ Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010). All power maths in this course is at 230 V.

questions.questionText: In Australia, when is a tight-fitting respirator fit-tested?
options: Only when it starts to feel loose
Before first use, then after facial changes
Never, as the wearer checks it daily
Only when the insurer says it must
questions.explanation: SafeWork SA: workers pass a fit test before first wearing a tight-fitting respirator, and again after a facial change that may affect the seal. Fit-check each time it goes on.

questions.questionText: What is the first step in the PPE removal order?
options: Clean soil off boots and outer gloves
Take the respirator off your face first
Take the inner gloves off your hands
Wash your face at the station first
questions.explanation: Knock off gross soil from boots and outer gloves first, then outer gloves, coverall inside out, boots, goggles, respirator by the straps, and inner gloves last.

questions.questionText: Why is the HVAC return in the work area switched off and sealed?
options: It draws too much power, 230 V
It makes the work area too cold
It interferes with the moisture meter readings
It would spread contamination through the ducts
questions.explanation: A return grille in the work area draws contaminated air through the ducted system and into the rest of the building. Seal it and switch it off before disturbance.

questions.questionText: Which material is usually cleaned, disinfected and kept?
options: Sewage-soaked carpet underlay
Wet ceiling insulation
Glazed ceramic tile
Soaked particleboard flooring
questions.explanation: Non-porous surfaces such as glazed tile can be cleaned and disinfected. Porous materials soaked with Category 3 water generally come out because cleaning cannot be verified.

questions.questionText: Two cleaning products are on the van. What is the rule?
options: Mix them for strength
Never mix the products
Mix if labels match
Mix them only outdoors
questions.explanation: Health authorities in both countries say never mix products. Mixing bleach with acids or ammonia-based cleaners can release dangerous gases.

questions.questionText: In New Zealand, what must you hold for each hazardous substance on site?
options: A current safety data sheet
An overseas product registration number
A receipt from the supplier
A photograph of the bottle
questions.explanation: WorkSafe New Zealand: it is mandatory to have a current SDS for each hazardous substance in the workplace. In Australia, SDS copies go in the hazardous chemicals register.

questions.questionText: Which is a lawful route for extracted Category 3 water?
options: The stormwater grate on the street
The garden bed beside the house
The street gutter late at night
A liquid-waste contractor with a docket
questions.explanation: Lawful routes are the sewer with the authority’s approval, or a liquid-waste contractor with a docket. Stormwater goes untreated to waterways.

questions.questionText: What does Sydney Water require before a business discharges commercial trade wastewater?
options: A verbal okay from the plumber
A photo of the drain cover
Formal approval from Sydney Water first
Nothing at all for small volumes
questions.explanation: Sydney Water says businesses must seek formal approval to discharge commercial trade wastewater. Other authorities have their own rules, so ask before you pump.

questions.questionText: Who may repair a broken sewer drain on a New Zealand property?
options: The restoration supervisor
An authorised drainlayer
The house occupant
Any site labourer
questions.explanation: The Plumbers, Gasfitters, and Drainlayers Act 2006 restricts drainlaying and sanitary plumbing to authorised people. In Australia it is licensed plumbing work.

questions.questionText: Mould is found on a Category 3 job before drying. What runs until it is cleared?
options: AFDs and dehumidifiers, not air movers
Air movers on the highest speed
Heaters running with the windows shut
Nothing until the insurer next visits
questions.explanation: The mould rule: contain, run AFDs and dehumidifiers to control moisture, remediate the mould, and bring in air movers only after cleaning and clearance.

questions.questionText: What do the Australian Consumer Law and NZ Consumer Guarantees Act both require of services?
options: A fixed price agreed in writing
Completion within one calendar week only
A written warranty of ten years
Due or reasonable care and skill
questions.explanation: The ACL guarantees services with due care and skill, fit for stated purpose. The NZ Consumer Guarantees Act requires reasonable care and skill and fitness for purpose.

questions.questionText: What decides that a Category 3 job is ready to hand over?
options: The carpet layer has been booked in
The odour has mostly gone by now
Recorded evidence it is clean and dry
The crew has run out of time
questions.explanation: Clearance is made on recorded evidence: contaminated material removed, surfaces clean, cleaning recorded, readings at the dry standard, photographs and a signed handover.
